claims.text: At high temperatures, the overall wear resistance of a FeNiCrCoCu thin coating is controlled by formation of a continuous, adherent surface oxide scale.
The oxide scale increases the coating-surface hardness.
The oxide scale reduces plastic deformation during sliding contact.
Reduced plastic deformation caused by the oxide scale lowers the wear rate.
The initial sputter-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating is homogeneous.
The initial FeNiCrCoCu coating is amorphous or nanocrystalline.
Exposure at 600–800°C in an oxidizing environment promotes formation of a protective oxide layer on FeNiCrCoCu.
Room-temperature or inert-atmosphere testing produces little or no oxide formation relative to high-temperature oxidizing exposure.
The surface scale will include chromium oxide and may include mixed copper-oxide phases.
Chromium preferentially oxidizes within FeNiCrCoCu at high temperature.
Thermal exposure can produce protective barrier coating layers that improve corrosion resistance.
The high-temperature oxide scale acts as a diffusion barrier.
The oxide scale reduces direct mechanical contact between the sliding bodies.
Reduced direct contact limits material removal under high-load sliding conditions.
An oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coating will have a lower wear rate than a room-temperature or inert-atmosphere baseline.
An oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coating will have a lower coefficient of friction than the baseline coating.
The proposed oxide-controlled wear mechanism is applicable over 600–800°C under loads typical of high-temperature applications.
Outside 600–800°C or under drastically different loads, other wear mechanisms may dominate.

contradictions.description: The main comparison permits a room-temperature baseline, which changes both temperature and oxidation, whereas the falsification experiment specifies a temperature-matched inert control that isolates oxidation. These are materially different baseline definitions.

The hypothesis and intervention describe in-situ oxide formation during high-temperature sliding, but the falsification design primarily forms the oxide by pre-aging before the wear test. Preformed and dynamically regenerated tribo-oxides need not test the same mechanism.
